page: Microsoft Azure E192s_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance supplies 192 dedicated virtual CPUs spanning 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by a 480 MB L3 cache. Total system memory measures 1536.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 for matrix computation. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, depending on remote storage attachment, and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show high parallel capacity, placing the multi-core stress-ng performance at 202122.5 and the PassMark CPU score at 152241.34, both in the top tier. Memory bandwidth delivers 688.47 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 271.22 GB/sec for writes. Database operations test in the top decile, complemented by Redis throughput of 251.49 million operations per second and static web throughput of 174.26 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core processing scores in the average range at 2290.89 in stress-ng, reflecting an architecture optimized for aggregate multi-threaded execution rather than high serial speed.

Qualitatively, the E192s_v7 delivers high compute and memory density per deployment, minimizing the architectural overhead of distributing large workloads across multiple smaller hosts. Because local storage is absent, storage performance relies on external block volumes. This server is aligned with in-memory databases, large-scale Redis clusters, large enterprise application backends, and intensive data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E192s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 192 dedicated vCPUs from 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 1536.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, alongside a 480 MB L3 cache and hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, utilizing network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark results place the instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU computation, PassMark database operations, and Redis throughput exceeding 251 million operations per second. Memory read bandwidth reaches 688.47 GB/sec on uncached blocks. Single-threaded performance sits in the middle tier, making the architecture best suited for heavily parallelized, memory-dense workloads such as in-memory databases, enterprise transactional systems, big data analytics, and large ETL data transformations.
